prompt:
An enzyme works well at $37\,^{\circ}\text{C}$. After the solution is heated to $80\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ and then cooled back to $37\,^{\circ}\text{C}$, the enzyme no longer functions.

Explain why the enzyme does not recover its activity.
teacher_notes: Full credit requires denaturation, loss of active site shape, and the link between shape and substrate binding. The phrase the enzyme died should be corrected, since enzymes are not alive.
sample_solution: Heating disrupted the weak interactions, such as hydrogen bonds and other side chain interactions, that hold the polypeptide in its folded three-dimensional shape, so the enzyme denatured. The active site's shape is what allows a specific substrate to bind, so once that shape is lost the enzyme can no longer form an enzyme-substrate complex and cannot lower the activation energy of the reaction. Cooling does not restore function because the unfolded chain does not reliably refold into its original conformation.
